stem:
Madhav draws transversal $n$ across lines $u$ and $v$. Angle $P$ sits below $u$ and to the left of $n$. Angle $Q$ sits below $v$ and to the left of $n$.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims about angles $P$ and $Q$ are correct?

options.text: Angles $P$ and $Q$ are corresponding angles, because each sits in the same matching position at its crossing.
Corresponding angles need one angle from the crossing with $u$ and one from the crossing with $v$.
Angles $P$ and $Q$ are corresponding angles even when both are taken from the crossing with $u$ alone.
Angles $P$ and $Q$ are same-side interior angles, so their measures must sum to $180^{\circ}$.

teacher.key_rationale: P and Q occupy matching lower-left positions at the two crossings, so they are corresponding; the pair needs one angle from each intersection. Taking both from u alone omits that condition. Treating them as same-side interior angles conflates a different pair.
